quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Give pedestrians the right-of-way only when the law says they have it.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way. This is true even if the pedestrian is crossing where they should not.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop right away and back up.
Driving conditions are not good.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not good.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that work is being done on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: Taking drugs along with alcohol:

options.text: Makes crashes more likely.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol less harmful to your driving.
Does not affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes crashes more likely.
questions.explanation: Drugs (including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter drugs) can hurt your brain function and make it hard to drive safely. Mixing alcohol with drugs makes crashes much more likely.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
The cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on the road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, what helps avoid crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Get off the highways quickly.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Slowing down and keeping more distance between cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on yellow background. They warn you about hazards ahead. This sign tells you a traffic light is coming. Be ready to stop for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in a crash because they are small.
Must never stand in a vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in a vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use proper car seats and safety belts for children.

questions.question: You are angry after something at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait before driving. Driving when emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not hit the brakes right away. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down by taking your foot off the gas. Once you are going very slowly, gently apply the brakes and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Opposing traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move your car into each lane as soon as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and safe to enter.

questions.question: What can lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces this risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns of a curve in the road ahead.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow center line. What does this tell you?

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
The road is under repair.
You must stay left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can cross it to pass when safe.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A road with restrictions on vehicle stereos.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: You stop at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks. What should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with multiple tracks, wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing. Another train may be approaching on a different track.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are in the wrong lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Put your vehicle in reverse and go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you become drowsy, pull over safely and rest or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns of hazards or dangers ahead.
It tells you a school zone is nearby.
It tells you a park or recreation area is nearby.
It tells you food and gas stations are ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards or dangers ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards and dangers. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle ahead has its lights flashing and is stopped. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down. If you can, change lanes to stay away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, change lanes to stay away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with lights flashing, you must change lanes if possible to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit. Always be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit sign show?

options.text: A suggested driving speed only.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed when weather and road conditions are good.
The maximum safe speed under all weather and road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed when weather and road conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road when conditions are ideal. You may need to drive slower when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected or hidden dangers.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you just came from.
The lane with an arrow marking.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you just came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and gently turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gently turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without hard braking and carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other traffic when you return to the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there are no other cars crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mark dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: You must come to a complete stop when you see which traffic light?

options.text: A flashing red light.
A steady yellow light.
A yellow arrow.
A flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You find a problem with your car that could make it unsafe to drive. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the problem right away.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem right away.
questions.explanation: Any problem that could affect safe driving must be fixed as soon as possible. Fix the problem before you drive.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: Cars drive faster at night.
There are more cars on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: It is harder to see at night. From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when people and cars cannot be seen from 500 feet away, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely into traffic when there is a safe gap.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way intersection controlled by stop signs:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way intersection, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, yield to the driver on your right. You may then proceed when it is safe.
